question: The Thermohaline Circulation directly influences which of the following crucial environmental factors all over the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The climate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Thermohaline Circulation" is the large-scale, deep-ocean circulation driven by differences in temperature (thermo) and salinity (haline), which control the density of sea water. By transporting heat from the equator towards the poles, it directly influences the climate all over the world. (तापलवणीय परिसंचरण — जलवायु को प्रभावित करता है)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It is often called the "global ocean conveyor belt" — a slow, continuous loop of deep and surface currents connecting all the oceans.

• The Gulf Stream/North Atlantic Drift, part of this system, keeps Western Europe much warmer than other regions at the same latitude.

• A slowdown of the thermohaline circulation (e.g., due to melting Arctic ice adding fresh water) could drastically change regional climates.

NOTE

• Ocean currents are caused by winds, the Earth's rotation (Coriolis force) and density differences (temperature + salinity). Warm currents: Gulf Stream, Kuroshio; cold currents: Labrador, Humboldt (Peru).

question: Name the social reformer of Bengal who played crucial role in the enactment of the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act 1856.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, the great social reformer and educationist of Bengal, campaigned relentlessly for widow remarriage, and his efforts led to the enactment of the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856 (passed by Lord Canning's government). (ईश्वरचंद्र विद्यासागर — विधवा पुनर्विवाह अधिनियम 1856)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Vidyasagar was Principal of Sanskrit College, Calcutta, promoted women's education (helped open many girls' schools) and simplified the Bengali alphabet/primer ("Barna Parichay").

• Other reform-law pairs: Raja Ram Mohan Roy — abolition of Sati (Regulation XVII, 1829, under Lord William Bentinck); B. M. Malabari — Age of Consent Act, 1891.

• Rabindranath Tagore was a poet (Nobel Prize 1913); Satyendra Nath Bose was a physicist; Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1897).

NOTE

• The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856, legalised the remarriage of Hindu widows in all jurisdictions of British India — passed just before the Revolt of 1857.

question: Teejan Bai is associated with which of the following dances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandvani.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Teejan Bai is the legendary exponent of "Pandavani (Pandvani)", the folk ballad-singing/performance tradition of Chhattisgarh in which episodes of the Mahabharata (tales of the Pandavas) are narrated with song, music and dramatic gestures. (तीजन बाई — पंडवानी, छत्तीसगढ़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Teejan Bai received the Padma Shri (1988), Padma Bhushan (2003) and Padma Vibhushan (2019), and also the Fukuoka Prize (2018).

• She performs in the vigorous Kapalik shaili of Pandavani, standing and moving with a tambura in hand.

• Option folk forms: Bagurumba — folk dance of the Bodo tribe (Assam); Garba — Gujarat; Jhumar — folk dance of Punjab/Rajasthan/Jharkhand region.

NOTE

• Famous folk-artist pairs for SSC: Teejan Bai — Pandavani; Bhikari Thakur — Bidesia (Bihar); Gulabo Sapera — Kalbelia (Rajasthan).

question: Several biological processes are catalysed by enzymes. Digestive enzymes are present in which part of the cell?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lysosomes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lysosomes" are membrane-bound cell organelles that contain powerful digestive (hydrolytic) enzymes. They break down worn-out organelles, food particles and foreign bodies like bacteria and viruses. (लाइसोसोम — पाचक एंजाइम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Lysosomes are called the "suicide bags of the cell" — when a cell is damaged, they burst and their enzymes digest the cell itself.

• They were discovered by Christian de Duve (Nobel Prize 1974) and are formed by the Golgi complex.

• Other organelles: Ribosomes — protein synthesis; Golgi complex — packaging and secretion; Mitochondria — "powerhouse of the cell" (ATP production).

NOTE

• Organelle nicknames for SSC: Mitochondria — powerhouse; Lysosome — suicide bag; Ribosome — protein factory; Nucleus — control room/brain of the cell.

question: What is the name of the process of organic matter being broken down into simpler compounds by decomposers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Decomposition.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Decomposition" is the process by which decomposers (bacteria, fungi) break down dead organic matter into simpler inorganic compounds, returning nutrients to the soil. (अपघटन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Decomposers (e.g., bacteria and fungi) are also called saprotrophs; earthworms and dung beetles that feed on detritus are detritivores.

• Decomposition is vital for nutrient cycling (nitrogen, carbon cycles) and soil fertility; steps include fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification and mineralisation.

• Photosynthesis — green plants make food using sunlight, CO₂ and water; Respiration — breakdown of glucose to release energy; Fermentation — anaerobic breakdown by microbes (e.g., yeast making alcohol).

NOTE

• In an ecosystem the flow is: Producers → Consumers → Decomposers. Decomposers are nature's recyclers — without them, dead matter and nutrients would remain locked up.

question: Which of the following is NOT true regarding the Swaran Singh Committee?
option_1: The committee was established during Indira Gandhi's Government
option_2: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act was based on its recommendations.
option_3: It suggested nine items as duties of the citizens.
option_4: The Swaran Singh Committee was set up in 1976.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It suggested nine items as duties of the citizens.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended eight Fundamental Duties, not nine. Acting on its recommendations, the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 added ten Fundamental Duties in a new Part IV-A (Article 51A). So the statement that it suggested "nine items" is NOT true. (स्वर्ण सिंह समिति — आठ मौलिक कर्तव्य सुझाए)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The committee was set up in 1976 during Indira Gandhi's government (Internal Emergency period) — so Options 1, 2 and 4 are true.

• The idea of Fundamental Duties is borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

• The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added the 11th Fundamental Duty — a parent/guardian to provide opportunities for education to the child between 6 and 14 years.

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts). Some committee suggestions (like penalty for non-compliance) were not accepted. Currently there are 11 Fundamental Duties under Article 51A (a) to (k).

question: Chip, Condor, Duff and Driver are some of the terms used in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Golf.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chip (a short lofted shot), Condor (four strokes under par — the rarest score), Duff (a badly mishit shot) and Driver (the club used for the longest shots from the tee) are all terms used in "Golf". (गोल्फ के शब्द)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other golf terms: Par, Birdie (1 under par), Eagle (2 under), Albatross (3 under), Bogey (1 over), Caddie, Tee, Bunker, Hole-in-one, Putt, Fairway.

• Famous Indian golfers: Anirban Lahiri, Jeev Milkha Singh, Aditi Ashok, Shubhankar Sharma.

• Terms of other options: Polo — chukker, mallet; Chess — checkmate, gambit, stalemate; Swimming — freestyle, butterfly, lap.

NOTE

• A standard golf course has 18 holes. The major tournaments (Majors): The Masters, PGA Championship, US Open, The Open (British Open).

question: Which ruler succeeded Chandragupta Maurya in 297 BCE?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bindusara.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bindusara, the son of Chandragupta Maurya, succeeded him around 297 BCE as the second ruler of the Maurya Empire. He was known to the Greeks as "Amitrochates" (Sanskrit: Amitraghata — "slayer of enemies"). (बिंदुसार — 297 ईसा पूर्व)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire (c. 321 BCE) with the help of Chanakya (Kautilya), author of the Arthashastra; in his last days he embraced Jainism and died at Shravanabelagola (Karnataka).

• Bindusara was succeeded by his son Ashoka the Great (c. 268 BCE), famous for the Kalinga War (261 BCE) and the spread of Buddhism.

• Kumaragupta was a Gupta ruler (founded Nalanda); Kanishka was the great Kushana king (Saka era, 78 CE).

NOTE

• Maurya succession: Chandragupta → Bindusara → Ashoka. Greek ambassador Megasthenes (author of "Indica") visited Chandragupta's court; Deimachus visited Bindusara's court.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, which state has the highest sex ratio?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, "Kerala" has the highest sex ratio among states — 1,084 females per 1,000 males. (केरल — 1084, सर्वाधिक लिंगानुपात)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The lowest sex ratio among states was in Haryana (879); among UTs, Daman and Diu (618) was the lowest, while Puducherry (1,037) was the highest among UTs.

• India's overall sex ratio (2011): 943 females per 1,000 males; child sex ratio (0–6 years): 919.

• Kerala also leads in literacy (94%) and human development indicators.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th Census (7th after Independence); its motto was "Our Census, Our Future". Census is conducted every 10 years under the Census Act, 1948 (Ministry of Home Affairs).

question: In 2023, the Government of India proposed 'Amrit Dharohar Scheme' to be implemented over the next _______________ to encourage optimal use of wetlands and enhance bio-diversity, carbon stock, eco-tourism opportunities and income generation for local communities.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Three Years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Amrit Dharohar Scheme", announced in the Union Budget 2023-24, is to be implemented over the next "three years" to encourage optimal use of wetlands, and enhance bio-diversity, carbon stock, eco-tourism opportunities and income generation for local communities. (अमृत धरोहर योजना — तीन वर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The scheme is run by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and focuses on the conservation of Ramsar wetland sites with community participation.

• Announced along with it in Budget 2023-24 was the "MISHTI" scheme (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes) for mangrove plantation.

• India has one of the largest networks of Ramsar sites (wetlands of international importance) in Asia; World Wetlands Day is observed on 2 February.

NOTE

• The Ramsar Convention on Wetlands was signed at Ramsar (Iran) in 1971. India joined it in 1982; Chilika Lake (Odisha) and Keoladeo National Park (Rajasthan) were India's first Ramsar sites.

question: In which of the following books has the author described the horrors of the holocaust and the Second World War?
option_1: The Diary of a young girl
option_2: I know why the caged bird sings
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Diary of a young girl.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Diary of a Young Girl" is the diary of Anne Frank, a Jewish girl who hid with her family in Amsterdam during the Nazi occupation. It describes the horrors of the Holocaust and the Second World War. (ऐनी फ्रैंक की डायरी — होलोकॉस्ट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Anne Frank wrote the diary (1942–1944) while hiding in the "Secret Annexe"; she died in the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp in 1945. Her father Otto Frank published the diary in 1947.

• The Holocaust was the genocide of about six million Jews by Nazi Germany under Adolf Hitler during World War II (1939–45).

• Other options: "I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings" — Maya Angelou; "Dreams from My Father" — Barack Obama; "Long Walk to Freedom" — Nelson Mandela.

NOTE

• International Holocaust Remembrance Day is observed on 27 January, the day the Auschwitz camp was liberated (1945).

question: Who among the following received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Amrit Award 2022 for Kuchipudi dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Smita Rajeshbhai Shastri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Smita Rajeshbhai Shastri received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Amrit Award 2022 for her contribution to "Kuchipudi" dance. (स्मिता राजेशभाई शास्त्री — कुचिपुड़ी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The SNA Amrit Award is a one-time award instituted in the year of "Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav" (75 years of Independence) to honour Indian artists above 75 years of age who had not yet received any national honour; 84 artists were conferred the award.

• Kuchipudi is the classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh, which originated in the village of Kuchipudi (Krishna district); famous exponents include Raja-Radha Reddy, Yamini Krishnamurthy and Vempati Chinna Satyam.

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi (established 1952/1953) is India's national academy for music, dance and drama.

NOTE

• Among the other names, Kumkum Lal (Odissi) and others received the Amrit Award for different art forms — the Kuchipudi awardee was Smita Shastri (of Gujarat).

question: Among the following Para athletes, which athlete is associated with the High Jump event?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mariyappan Thangavelu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mariyappan Thangavelu (Tamil Nadu) is India's celebrated Para high jumper. He won gold in the men's high jump (T-42) at the Rio 2016 Paralympics, silver at Tokyo 2020 and bronze at Paris 2024. (मरियप्पन थंगावेलु — ऊँची कूद)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Avani Lekhara — Para shooting (first Indian woman to win a Paralympic gold — 10m Air Rifle, Tokyo 2020; defended it in Paris 2024).

• Deepa Malik — shot put (first Indian woman to win a Paralympic medal — silver, Rio 2016); later President of the Paralympic Committee of India.

• Ajeet Singh Yadav — Para javelin throw (silver at Paris 2024 Paralympics).

• Mariyappan received the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2020) and Padma Shri (2017).

NOTE

• Other Indian Paralympic stars: Devendra Jhajharia (javelin, 2 golds), Sumit Antil (javelin gold, Tokyo & Paris), Krishna Nagar (badminton gold).

question: M Balamuralikrishna was awarded Padma Vibhushan in 1991 for which of the following fields?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carnatic music.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. M. Balamuralikrishna (1930–2016) was a legendary vocalist of "Carnatic music" (the classical music of South India). He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 1991 for his contribution to Carnatic music. (एम. बालमुरलीकृष्ण — कर्नाटक संगीत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A child prodigy from Andhra Pradesh, he composed in all 72 Melakarta ragas, created new ragas, and received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and France's Chevalier of the Ordre des Arts et des Lettres.

• The Trinity of Carnatic music: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri.

• Hindustani music is the North Indian classical tradition (e.g., Pt. Bhimsen Joshi, Ustad Bismillah Khan).

NOTE

• Padma Vibhushan is India's second-highest civilian award (after Bharat Ratna). Carnatic music concerts typically feature the violin, mridangam and ghatam as accompaniments.

question: The Union Territory of Puducherry is located in which of the following river basins?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kaveri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Union Territory of "Puducherry" (its main region on the Coromandel coast) lies in the "Kaveri (Cauvery) river basin" — distributaries of the Kaveri delta region flow through it. (पुडुचेरी — कावेरी बेसिन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Kaveri rises at Talakaveri (Brahmagiri hills, Coorg, Karnataka) and flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu into the Bay of Bengal; it is called the "Ganga of the South".

• Puducherry UT consists of four unconnected districts: Puducherry and Karaikal (Tamil Nadu coast), Yanam (Andhra Pradesh — Godavari delta) and Mahe (Kerala coast). It was a French colony until its de facto transfer to India in 1954.

• Tributaries of the Kaveri: Hemavati, Kabini, Bhavani, Amaravati; the Sivasamudram Falls and Mettur Dam are on it.

NOTE

• The Kaveri water dispute involves Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry — settled through the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal and monitored by the Cauvery Water Management Authority.

question: 0.25 g of an organic compound gave 0.13 g of water after complete combustion. The percentage composition of hydrogen is _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.78%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In combustion analysis (Liebig's method), all the hydrogen of the organic compound is converted into water (H₂O). The formula is:

◦ % of Hydrogen = (2/18) × (mass of H₂O / mass of compound) × 100

• Here, mass of water = 0.13 g and mass of compound = 0.25 g:

◦ % H = (2/18) × (0.13/0.25) × 100 = (0.26/18) × 400 = 5.78% (approx.)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Molecular mass of H₂O = 18; it contains 2 g of hydrogen per 18 g of water — hence the factor 2/18 (= 1/9).

• Similarly, % of Carbon = (12/44) × (mass of CO₂ / mass of compound) × 100, since CO₂ (mol. mass 44) contains 12 g carbon.

NOTE

• Liebig's combustion method estimates C and H; Kjeldahl's method estimates nitrogen; Carius method estimates halogens and sulphur — a favourite SSC chemistry fact set.

question: Which house is considered as lower house in State Legislature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vidhan Sabha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a State Legislature, the "Vidhan Sabha (Legislative Assembly)" is the lower house — the directly elected, more powerful house. The Vidhan Parishad (Legislative Council) is the upper house in states that have a bicameral legislature. (विधान सभा — निचला सदन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Members of the Vidhan Sabha (MLAs) are directly elected; its maximum strength is 500 and minimum 60 (Article 170); term is 5 years; minimum age to contest is 25 years.

• Only six states currently have a Legislative Council (bicameral): Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh (Article 169 governs its creation/abolition).

• At the Union level, the Lok Sabha is the lower house and the Rajya Sabha the upper house of Parliament.

NOTE

• A Money Bill in a state can be introduced only in the Vidhan Sabha; the Vidhan Parishad can delay it for a maximum of 14 days.

question: Who built an elegant two-storey ‘ship palace’ between two reservoirs named Jahaaz Mahal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sultan Ghiyasuddin Khilji.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Jahaz Mahal (Ship Palace)" at Mandu (Madhya Pradesh) was built by Sultan Ghiyasuddin Khilji (Ghiyas-ud-din Khalji) of Malwa (r. 1469–1500). The elegant two-storey palace stands on a narrow strip of land between two reservoirs — Munj Talao and Kapur Talao — so that it appears to float like a ship. (जहाज़ महल — मांडू, गयासुद्दीन ख़िलजी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It is said to have housed the sultan's large harem; its ship-like reflection in the lakes gives it the name "ship palace".

• Other monuments at Mandu: Hindola Mahal ("swinging palace"), Rani Roopmati's Pavilion, Baz Bahadur's Palace, Hoshang Shah's Tomb (India's first marble tomb, said to have inspired the Taj Mahal), Jami Masjid.

• Do not confuse the Malwa sultan Ghiyasuddin Khilji with the Delhi sultans Alauddin Khalji or Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.

NOTE

• Mandu (Mandavgad), in the Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh, was the capital of the Malwa Sultanate and is famous for the romance of Baz Bahadur and Rani Roopmati.

question: Who among the following was the Sultan of Delhi when Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347 CE?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347 CE by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu/Zafar Khan), when nobles of the Deccan revolted against the Delhi Sultan "Muhammad bin Tughlaq" (r. 1325–1351). (बहमनी साम्राज्य — 1347, मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक के शासनकाल में)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Bahmani capital was first at Gulbarga (Ahsanabad) and later shifted to Bidar. The kingdom eventually split into the five Deccan Sultanates: Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar, Bidar and Berar.

• During the same reign, the Vijayanagara Empire (founded 1336 by Harihara and Bukka) also arose in the south.

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq is known for the transfer of the capital to Daulatabad, the token copper currency, and ambitious taxation in the Doab — all of which failed; the traveller Ibn Battuta visited his court.

NOTE

• The famous Persian scholar Mahmud Gawan was the great wazir of the later Bahmani kingdom; his madrasa still stands at Bidar.

question: According to Census of India 2011, in which of the following Union Territories was the sex ratio recorded at 1037 females per 1000 males?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Puducherry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, the Union Territory of "Puducherry" recorded a sex ratio of 1,037 females per 1,000 males — the highest among all Union Territories (and the only UT above 1,000). (पुडुचेरी — 1037)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Sex ratios of the other option UTs (2011): Andaman & Nicobar — 876; Chandigarh — 818; Lakshadweep — 946. The lowest among UTs was Daman & Diu (618).

• Among states, Kerala (1,084) had the highest and Haryana (879) the lowest sex ratio.

• India's overall sex ratio in 2011 was 943.

NOTE

• Sex ratio in India is defined as the number of females per 1,000 males. Census 2011 was the 15th census; the next census has been delayed beyond 2021.

question: In which of the following cities of India was the first successful textile mill established?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first successful (modern) cotton textile mill in India was established in 1854 at Bombay (Mumbai) by the Parsi entrepreneur Cowasjee Nanabhoy Davar (Bombay Spinning and Weaving Mill). (पहली सफल सूती मिल — मुंबई, 1854)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The very first cotton mill (unsuccessful) was set up in 1818 at Fort Gloster, near Kolkata.

• Mumbai and Ahmedabad became the great centres of the cotton textile industry — Mumbai is called the "Cottonopolis of India"; Ahmedabad the "Manchester of India".

• Reasons for Mumbai's success: humid coastal climate (threads do not break), cotton from the Deccan black-soil belt, port facilities, capital and market.

• The first jute mill was set up at Rishra (near Kolkata) in 1855.

NOTE

• Textiles is India's classic agro-based industry; the sector is a major employer after agriculture — a frequently asked SSC economic-geography fact.

question: Which of the following Acts was provided for the establishment of a federal court in India?
option_2: The Government of India Act of 1935
option_4: The Government of India Act of 1919
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Government of India Act of 1935.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Government of India Act, 1935" provided for the establishment of a Federal Court in India, which was set up in 1937 at Delhi with Sir Maurice Gwyer as its first Chief Justice. (भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1935 — संघीय न्यायालय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The 1935 Act also provided for an All-India Federation, provincial autonomy (abolishing dyarchy in provinces and introducing it at the Centre), a Federal Bank (RBI, 1935), and separation of subjects into Federal, Provincial and Concurrent lists.

• The Federal Court was replaced by the Supreme Court of India on 28 January 1950.

• Regulating Act, 1773 — established the Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774); Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley–Minto) — separate electorates for Muslims; GoI Act, 1919 (Montagu–Chelmsford) — dyarchy in provinces.

NOTE

• Our Constitution borrowed a large number of provisions from the Government of India Act, 1935 — federal scheme, office of Governor, emergency provisions, Public Service Commissions and judiciary details.

question: Which of the following is NOT included in the national income?
option_1: Income received by a person as a donation
option_2: Income received by a household for the use of their entrepreneurial skill
option_3: Income received by a person for the use of his capital
option_4: Income received by a household for the use of their land
solution_text:
The correct answer is Income received by a person as a donation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• National income includes only factor incomes — payments received for supplying the factors of production: rent (land), wages (labour), interest (capital) and profit (entrepreneurship).

• A "donation" is a transfer payment — money received without any productive service in return — and transfer payments are NOT included in national income. (दान — हस्तांतरण भुगतान, राष्ट्रीय आय में शामिल नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are factor incomes: entrepreneurial skill → profit, capital → interest, land → rent — all counted in national income.

• Other transfer payments excluded from national income: old-age pensions, scholarships, unemployment allowance, gifts, remittances, lottery winnings.

• National income (NNP at factor cost) = GDP + Net factor income from abroad − Depreciation − Net indirect taxes.

NOTE

• Rule of thumb for SSC: if no good or service is produced in exchange, the receipt is a transfer income and stays out of national income; also excluded are sale of second-hand goods and windfall gains.

question: Jon Beel mela is held every year in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Jonbeel (Jon Beel) Mela" is a unique three-day community fair held every year in January (after Magh Bihu) at Dayang Belguri, Morigaon district of Assam. (जोनबील मेला — असम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Its most remarkable feature is the ancient barter system — tribal communities from the hills (Tiwa, Karbi, Khasi, Jaintia) exchange their produce with the people of the plains without using money.

• "Jonbeel" means a crescent-moon-shaped wetland (beel) — jon = moon, beel = wetland/lake — beside which the fair is held.

• The fair is patronised by the Tiwa (Lalung) king (Gobha Raja), who symbolically collects taxes from his subjects during the mela.

NOTE

• Famous festivals of Assam: Bihu (Rongali/Bohag, Bhogali/Magh, Kongali/Kati), Ambubachi Mela (Kamakhya, Guwahati), Majuli Raas and Jonbeel Mela — regulars in SSC art-and-culture questions.

question: Proposed in 2023-24, which section of the Income Tax Act of 1961 exempts senior citizens aged 75 years and above from filing income tax returns?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Section 194P.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Section 194P" of the Income Tax Act, 1961 exempts senior citizens aged 75 years and above from filing income tax returns, provided they have only pension income and interest income from the same specified bank, which deducts the applicable tax itself. (धारा 194P — 75 वर्ष से अधिक वरिष्ठ नागरिकों को रिटर्न भरने से छूट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Section 194P was inserted by the Finance Act, 2021 (effective 1 April 2021) to reduce the compliance burden on very senior citizens.

• Other sections: Section 139A — Permanent Account Number (PAN); Section 234C — interest for deferment of advance tax; Section 80C — deduction up to Rs. 1.5 lakh for investments (LIC, PPF, ELSS, etc.).

• Under the Act, a "senior citizen" is 60+ years and a "super/very senior citizen" is 80+ years for slab purposes.

NOTE

• The Income Tax Act was enacted in 1961; income tax in India was first introduced by Sir James Wilson in 1860. Direct taxes are administered by the CBDT under the Ministry of Finance.
